result.behaviour_summary: New rule module idx-signals/idxsig/rules/moonshot_e5.py (numpy/pandas only, module-level literals only, audit passes) implementing the protocol draft's "family" section. features() returns names x sessions float arrays: ret1, rel1, ret5, ret20, volr, brk60, dd60, cpos, gap copied verbatim from moonshot_g.features; valr, rngr, vol20, up5, zero20, age, logval20 copied verbatim from e1.Study._signals (vol20 is Study's definition: a present-but-untraded session is a zero log return, which is what the E1/E2 signal tables used; moonshot_g's vol20 drops those sessions instead); ara = lock_up & tradeable as moonshot_e1. age and zero20 are NaN before a name's first present session (Study leaves them negative / 0 there; after listing they equal Study's values exactly, zero20 = 0 at listing because pre-listing sessions are not present). Pre-spike block: creep5v20 = median(volume t-4..t)/median(volume t-24..t-5) over present sessions with untraded = 0 volume (full windows required); rngr5 = median(rngr t-4..t); vc10_60 = vol10/vol60 (rolling std of Study's log-return series, min_periods 8 and 45, the 0.75 ratio vol20 uses); quiet = (rngr5 <= 1.0) & (|ret5| <= 2*vol20*sqrt(5)); not_repriced = ret20 < 0.30; rebase = exists s0 in [t-40, t-6] with spike(s0), level(t) <= pre + 0.5*(peak - pre), min level(t-4..t) >= pre, where pre = level(s0-1), peak = max level(s0..t), spike = (ret1 >= 0.30) | (lock_up & tradeable) (equal to ret1 >= 0.30 on US/CRYPTO where lock_up is identically False; on IDX the ARA lock is the spike, plus any literal +30% close in the sub-Rp200 band). Every window is trailing; column s uses sessions <= s only. rank_features: per-session (rank-0.5)/n percentile among present & tradeable names, masked by present before ranking, NaN -> 0.5, plus squared ranks, binaries 0/1. WARMUP = 60: every features()/rank_features() array and compute() is NaN in the first 60 columns of the view (a view shorter than 60 columns is all NaN). score() = logit over FEATURE_ORDER; Arm A = logit_U, Arm B = logit_U - logit_D; flags()/debounce(): a flag only on the first session the score is >= threshold after >= 5 consecutive sessions outside the set (a NaN score counts as outside; nothing before 5 sessions of history; prefix-safe). A0_CREEP_QUIET = creep5v20 >= 1.5 & quiet (the KOD-DET-v0 VOLUME_CREEP_PRICE_QUIET conjunction, verified against price_facts.measures()), A1 = A0 & not_repriced; the registered A0/A1 rules are debounced the same way. Literals COEF_U/COEF_D/INTERCEPT_U/INTERCEPT_D/THRESHOLD_A/THRESHOLD_B are tuple-of-pairs per market, all None, SELECTED = None. Unfrozen behaviour (stated): family_flags(f) returns all-False for an arm whose literals are None (so e1.Study / a feature table can be built), while the registered candidate rule's compute() RAISES RuntimeError naming the arm and the word 'frozen' (a harness run on an unfrozen ranker is an error, never a silent zero-signal run); A0/A1 always compute. rules/__init__.py: moonshot_e5 appended to registry()'s module tuple, additive only. compute() returns np.where(tradeable, flag, NaN) with the first 60 columns NaN, 0/1/NaN only; rules.causal_signals passes (prefix-first, sandbox, audit) for a frozen arm (synthetic literals patched in the test) and for A0/A1.

result.defaults_unchanged_evidence: Only additive changes: a new module, a new test file, and moonshot_e5 appended to the module tuple in rules.registry(). No existing argument, column, key, default, rule text or threshold was touched. The `python3 -m idxsig rules` listing shows every pre-existing rule hash identical before and after (e.g. MOONSHOT_E1_D1 648a06e1079f, MOONSHOT_E2_US_D1 c21126d8ba9d, MOONSHOT_E2_CRYPTO_D1 d8218f2e9c9b, MOONSHOT_E4_D1 f5585be5d967, E3_CAND_F8_ARA_EARLY 2c5e91686ff3, E4_CAND_G2_RET30 362a9207a418, PLACEBO_COINFLIP b774201b08e6), so every recorded run's rule_sha256 still resolves (verify-runs: OK). The 244 pre-existing tests pass unchanged (262 = 244 + 18 new). Rule hashes cover each module's own source, and rules/__init__.py is not part of any rule hash. git show --stat: __init__.py 4 lines (+2/-2 import and tuple), everything else new files. test_e5_rules asserts the E5 copies of ret1/rel1/ret5/ret20/volr/dd60/cpos/gap/brk60 equal moonshot_g.features and valr/rngr/vol20/up5/logval20 equal e1.Study.sig, i.e. E5 reuses the recorded definitions rather than altering them.
needs_other_file: idx-signals/idxsig/e1.py:190 (Study._signals): `flags[next(k for k in flags if "IGNITION" in k)]` raises StopIteration for the E5 family (no IGNITION member); the draft already lists 'guard the IGNITION lookup (line 190)' as an e1.py change, needed before e5.py builds labels via e1.Study with family_module=moonshot_e5. Study itself instantiates fine on a synthetic panel with the E1 family (verified).

idx-signals/idxsig/e5.py (new, not mine): Stage 1/2 must score discovery-fitted coefficients before the literals are frozen; the module exposes score(), flags(), detector_states(), rank_features()/features() for that, but a registered E5_CAND_<MARKET>_<ARM> rule refuses to compute until the literals are committed, so Stage-2 harness runs need either the freeze first (as the draft's stage 3 says) or an e5.py-built Rule carrying the discovery coefficients.

research/E5/protocol.json (freeze, not mine): should state the module's concrete choices listed under open_concerns (rank formula, vol20 variant, vc10_60 min_periods, rebase pre/peak, IDX spike union, NaN-counts-as-outside debounce, one FEATURE_ORDER for all markets).
open_concerns: IDX spike for `rebase`: implemented as (ret1 >= 0.30) | (lock_up & tradeable), identical to the draft on US/CRYPTO (lock_up is all False there) but on IDX a superset of the draft's 'lock_up & tradeable' (it also counts a literal +30% close in the sub-Rp200 band, where 35% limits allow one). A rule cannot know its market, so a market-agnostic definition was needed; the protocol should either adopt this union or specify how the IDX form is selected.

vol20 follows e1.Study._signals (present-but-untraded session = 0 log return), not moonshot_g.features (such sessions dropped); the two differ only on IDX names with untraded sessions. The quiet band and vc10_60 use the same series. Chosen because the E1/E2 signal_stats tables were computed from Study._signals.
vc10_60 min_periods (8 of 10, 45 of 60) are my choice (vol20's 15/20 ratio); the draft does not specify them.

rebase: pre = level(s0-1), peak = max level(s0..t), 'exists any s0 in [t-40, t-6]'; the draft names the three conditions but not pre/peak explicitly. A missing (non-present) session anywhere in s0-1..t makes the test fail for that s0 (np.maximum propagates NaN).

creep5v20 requires full windows (5 and 20 present sessions); a name with a presence gap in t-24..t has NaN creep (rank 0.5, A0 False). price_facts.py instead drops bars with missing fields and re-indexes; identical on gap-free series (tested), different across gaps.

Debounce convention: a NaN score (warm-up, not evaluable) counts as 'outside' the top set, and nothing flags before 5 sessions of history; so columns 60..64 of a view can flag. Every harness window starts 60 sessions before its period, so this never touches a period session; stated here because the draft's 'outside it' wording could also be read as 'five evaluable sessions below'.
Percentile rank formula (rank - 0.5)/n with average ties (midrank; a single-name pool ranks 0.5); the draft says 'percentile rank' without the formula. Ranks fall in (0, 1), not [0, 1].

One FEATURE_ORDER (41 columns) for all markets: gap on IDX ranks 0.5 everywhere and ara off IDX is 0 everywhere, constant columns the e5.py fit must tolerate (L2 ridge keeps them finite); alternatively e5.py could zero their coefficients.

The candidate rule for an unfrozen arm raises rather than returning all-False (deliberate: no silent zero-signal harness run); family_flags() returns all-False for it so e1.Study and paper-style feature tables still build. Both behaviours are tested.

Rule hash: the per-market literals are inside the module source, so freezing them (stage 3) changes every E5 rule's sha, including A0/A1's, which is the intended 'rule hash covers them' but means A0/A1 discovery-stage runs recorded before the freeze will carry a different sha than post-freeze runs.
